A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same explainability-guided token-compression work despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression experiments across three MLLMs, including benchmark evaluations, an aggregation ablation, generalization tests, and qualitative case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark evaluations, compressor-design ablations, and inference-time and memory measurements.

M1.justification: Equation 1 now explicitly takes the positive part of attention-gradient products before aggregation; v1 lacks this operation. The convolutional mapper, first-layer input, label masking, KL objective, and pruning procedure otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish a revision to the stated rule, not whether the executed implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds POPE, TextVQA, and MMBench in Table 2, plus GQA, ScienceQA, VizWiz, ChartQA, DocVQA, and OCRBench in Appendix F, Table 8. These substantially broaden hallucination, scientific reasoning, accessibility, and text/document/chart evaluation. Training sources and video-task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The main image and video comparisons expand from FastV to FastV, PyramidDrop, and Dart, including the 10% retention comparisons. PyramidDrop previously appeared only in a limited MMStar comparison. FastVID, PruneVID, and VisionZip remain in the separate MVBench comparison.

E3.justification: Main comparisons change FastV pruning from layer 4 to layer 2 to target comparable FLOPs. v2 adds total/prefill-time and KV-cache evaluation and controlled depth/input-layer experiments. Reported image-token counts for LLaVA-OneVision/Qwen2-VL also change from 1500/1849 to 1849/1500; this is a reported setting revision without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds ablations testing convolutional depths of 3, 5, 7, and 10 layers and attention inputs from layers 1, 2, 4, and 6. These investigate capacity and the accuracy-cost tradeoff beyond v1's aggregation ablation. Existing case studies, larger-input generalization, and 10% video-compression analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Benchmark-averaged performance preservation is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, comparator, ablation, timing, and memory results. Most shared scores for the proposed compressor remain unchanged; replaced FastV scores use revised pruning settings. Figure 3 also changes PruneVID's MVBench preservation from 96.7% to 99.1%, matching the retained table value. New Table 6 contains identical score rows with conflicting averages.

T1.justification: The positive-part operation in Equation 1 is a non-equivalent mathematical revision. New Appendix A defines that operation and elaborates GAE/R-GAE relevance propagation. The remaining core equations and FLOPs calculations are retained, and no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds an explicit claim to be among the earliest investigations of pre-LLM task-related compression and foregrounds that framing. The central contributions—input-stage pruning, learning from explainability, and generalization across MLLMs—remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: The new discussion explains shallow-attention usefulness and learning important regions rather than an exact relevance map. Appendix E adds capacity/overfitting interpretations and arguments for the first-layer efficiency tradeoff. Existing interpretations concerning video redundancy and the resource-intensive generation of relevance labels remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies A100 80GB evaluation hardware, exact channel configurations for new depth ablations, and GQA-aware KV-cache accounting. Most optimizer, training-data, filtering, epoch, and inference details already existed and move into Appendix C. No new code-access resource is provided.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Dart, DivPrune, Grad-SAM, and the additional benchmark papers, and clarifies the relationship to GAE/R-GAE. It emphasizes complementarity with built-in task-agnostic compression while retaining the original related-work taxonomy and overall positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from Generic to Task-Related Token Compression, with corresponding revisions to motivation and terminology. Implementation details move from Section 4.1 into Appendix C, and appendices are reorganized. The main section sequence and substantial portions of the exposition remain.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redesigned into radar charts and a FLOPs/performance comparison. Figure 2 reuses the vapor example already present in the appendices. Comparison tables gain baseline rows and FLOPs/task columns, new ablation and efficiency tables are added, and the conference template changes captions, typography, and layout.

improvement.justification: Broader task coverage, stronger comparator coverage, and direct timing/KV-cache measurements better support generality and practical efficiency than v1's primarily accuracy-and-FLOPs evidence. However, new reporting inconsistencies temper the gains: Table 6 assigns different averages to identical 25%-retention score rows, weakening its depth-ablation conclusions. The net improvement is supported but limited.
